text:
alex_p: Heads-up — ran a short lab run mixing tiny 10–30 token requests with long streaming ones. Seeing repeated micro-sleeps in the continuous-batcher and bump in 95p for long requests. wanted to loop you all in.

maria_r: ugh that pattern again. can you share traces? :eyes:

alex_p: pasted a condensed flame in the ticket. TL;DR: coalesce wait ~5–7ms on micro-window, and when tenant churn is high those sleeps stack and push 95p by ~3–6ms for streaming routes.

jia: is this the old "sleepers" we saw or new because of lease handoff churn?

samuel: i suspect interplay with lease reassigns + fencing. when a slot fences, small reqs enqueue but wait until kv attach, causing micro-waits.

maria_r: quick mitigation thought: fast-path for tiny requests (<= N tokens) that bypasses coalesce when runtime util < threshold. disabled under high util to avoid packing loss.

alex_p: prototyped `microfast=true` locally. improved median/tail for small requests but we paid in pack efficiency for medium-size traffic — tokens/s dropped.

jia: classic latency vs throughput. need unit-cost numbers. if tokens/s drops >5% for small tail win it's often not worth it unless SLA mandates.

samuel: alternate: weaken queue-fence semantics. allow enqueue optimism: mark items as probation if lease uncertain and allow them to be mixed into in-flight batches under conditions.

maria_r: probation path sounds interesting but operationally complex. sketch it?

samuel: sketch: `lease_token` optional. missing token -> mark `probation`. when coalescing, permit probation items only if batch_deadline < X ms and total_tokens < pack_limit. on move-confirm, noop. on failure, reprioritize or reroute.

alex_p: failure modes: duplicates across slots, kv cache misses, more noisy telemetry. we'd need short-lived dedupe and stronger idempotency tokens.

jia: dedupe table helps duplicates but KV prefix misses are painful; would need opportunistic cache-warming or accept extra latency for those items.

maria_r: can we be observability-first: add metrics (micro-sleeps/sec, fence-events, probation-enqueues, pack-efficiency) and tags (`enqueue_hint=probation|steady`) before adding control paths?

alex_p: yes. i'll add `enqueue_hint` span tag and a couple counters to canary. then run an experiment matrix.

samuel: experiment plan proposal: 1) 48h baseline (telemetry only) 2) enable microfast on 5% machines for 48h 3) enable probation on 5% machines for 48h. keep traffic slice identical.

jia: add derived unit-cost: tokens/s per GPU and tail latency per request-size bucket. decision rule example: reject microfast if tokens/s loss >5% unless 95p improves >10ms.

maria_r: also try hybrid heuristic: microfast only for tenants with high interarrival variance (burstiness). classify by IoD over recent window.

alex_p: lab config I used: 
```nnbatcher:
  microfast_threshold_tokens: 40
  microfast_enable_if_util_below: 0.6
  probation_enabled: false
  probation_deadline_ms: 12
```

samuel: nice. when mixing probation into batches we should emit `mixed_probation_batches` and track downstream failure/cold-cache rate so we can correlate.

jia: rollout plan: telemetry -> offline analysis -> small canary for microfast -> measure tokens/s and tails -> decide on probation. keep probation off until we understand cost.

alex_p: i'll open a follow-up doc (RFC style) with telemetry fields and experiment matrix. deploying tags to canary now.

maria_r: add console shortcut to surface tenants with high micro-sleep ratio for QE/support triage.

samuel: ping me when dashboard exists and i'll wire the mixed_probation metric.

opsbot: Deployed: tracing/enqueue_hint tagging to canary fleet at 5205004444 — rollout 10%.

maria_r: perfect. sync next week after 48h run?

jia: works for me.

samuel: yep.

alex_p: thanks all, closing thread for now; will post RFC link when ready.
